What we check

Six data sources.
One plain English report.

Every paid report pulls from six official UK sources and explains the findings so you understand what you are looking at, no financial background needed.

🏛

Company Overview

Status, incorporation date, company type, SIC code, overdue accounts, and overdue confirmation statements. The first signal that something is wrong.

📡 Companies House
⚡

Registered Charges

Who has a legal claim over this company's assets and what type of charge they hold. Fixed, floating, negative pledge. In plain English, not legal jargon.

📡 Companies House
🔴

Insolvency Records

CVL, administration, compulsory winding up. We surface the type, name the practitioners, and tell you what it means for unpaid invoices.

📡 Companies House
👤

Officers & Directors

Who is in control, how long they have been appointed, whether they have resigned recently, and whether identity verification is outstanding.

📡 Companies House
⚖️

County Court Judgements

How many CCJs are registered, total value, claimants, and whether they have been satisfied. A pattern of unsatisfied CCJs is one of the clearest warning signs.

📡 Registry Trust
🏅

Fair Payment Code

Has this company publicly committed to paying suppliers on time? We check the Small Business Commissioner's register and show their tier.

Nexora Digital Solutions Ltd IN LIQUIDATION
🔴 Insolvency case ⚠ Charge registered 🔴 Accounts overdue

Our Summary

Nexora Digital Solutions Ltd is a private limited IT consultancy incorporated in June 2020, currently in liquidation. The company entered Creditors Voluntary Liquidation on 26 February 2024 following an extraordinary resolution to wind up. An outstanding charge registered in August 2021 in favour of Swishfund LTD covers all assets under a fixed and floating arrangement, including a negative pledge. The company's last filed accounts covered the period to May 2022.

Charges & Insolvency

Know who has a claim on this company's assets.

A company with an outstanding charge has pledged its assets to a lender. A company in liquidation cannot legally pay you. Both are in the public record. InvoiceGuard surfaces both, with a clear explanation of what it means for your invoice.

Fixed and floating charges explained in plain English, not legal language
Insolvency type, commencement date, and appointed practitioners surfaced clearly
Negative pledge flags: when a company is legally barred from taking on more debt
See full report →
Registered Charges 1 Outstanding
Charge HolderSwishfund LTD
StatusOutstanding
Created17 August 2021
Charge TypeFixed + Floating
Negative PledgeYes

Our Interpretation

Swishfund LTD holds a charge over all assets of this company, including a floating charge and a negative pledge. This means the lender ranks ahead of unsecured creditors, including holders of unpaid invoices, in any distribution of assets.

CCJs & Fair Payment Code

Two data sources your competitors don't combine.

County Court Judgements tell you whether a company has been ordered by a court to pay a debt and refused. The Fair Payment Code tells you whether they've made a public commitment to pay suppliers promptly. InvoiceGuard checks both.

CCJ count, total value, claimants, and satisfaction status from the Registry Trust
Fair Payment Code tier, Gold, Silver, Bronze, or none, from the Small Business Commissioner
Both included in every paid report, no extra charge, no separate search

Filing History

The full story of a company in one timeline.

A company's filing history is a chronological record of everything it has ever submitted to Companies House. InvoiceGuard reads that timeline, colour-codes the events that matter, and tells you what the pattern means.

Red flags including missed accounts, winding-up resolutions, and charge registrations highlighted automatically
Gaps in filing detected. A company that stopped filing before it went insolvent is a warning sign

The real cost of not checking

They were already in trouble
before they hired you.

The client looked legitimate. The website was professional. What you did not know, sitting in the public record the entire time, was that the company had an outstanding charge, accounts two years overdue, and a winding-up resolution filed three weeks before they contacted you.

01A company in liquidation cannot pay your invoice. Your debt joins a queue and unsecured creditors are last.
02Overdue accounts and missed confirmation statements are public warning signs, visible for free, that most people never think to check.
03A company with three unsatisfied CCJs before they hire you is telling you exactly what kind of client they will be.

Questions answered.

The free search shows you the company's basic public profile: status, incorporation date, company type, and key signals like whether an insolvency case or charge is on record. It does not show the detail behind those signals, director names, CCJ data, or the full written summary. That is what the paid report unlocks.
No. Credits never expire. Buy a pack when you need it and use your reports at your own pace, whether that is over a week or a year. There is no subscription to cancel.
Every report pulls from Companies House (company status, charges, insolvency, officers, filing history), Registry Trust (County Court Judgements), and the Small Business Commissioner (Fair Payment Code). All are official UK public registers. Our written summary is generated by InvoiceGuard using that data and never adds information that is not in the public record.
No. Our written summary translates public register data into plain English. It does not constitute legal, financial, or credit advice. InvoiceGuard is an intelligence tool that gives you the information to make your own informed decision. For specific legal or financial advice, always consult a qualified professional.
Companies House gives you raw data across multiple pages. InvoiceGuard pulls it all into one report, adds CCJ data and Fair Payment Code status that Companies House does not cover, and gives you a plain English summary under every section so you understand what you are looking at even without a financial background.
InvoiceGuard searches the Companies House register, which covers registered limited companies and LLPs. Sole traders and general partnerships are not registered at Companies House and cannot be searched.
